epic.title: cleanup-e-crew-tooling
epic.intent_and_why: Two defects in crew tooling, same file, same subsystem, both about a crew's run being legible to everyone else while it happens: #607 (a blocked-but-healthy parent going lease-stale) and #525 (concurrent crews colliding on shared scratch evidence).

definition_of_done: A blocked parent that used to read stale no longer does, driven through the real registry and staleness path.
Two crews whose evidence used to collide no longer do, plus a loud error surface when a collision is genuinely forced.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Independent-reviewer APPROVE per gate, full clean-env cache-cleared suite green
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Real fresh-process integration checks against the real checklist engine and registry, not reasoned about from inside the authoring session
good_enough.appetite: One working session, two bounded gates

hard_constraints: No edit to scripts/checklist_engine.py, scripts/gauge_reader.py, scripts/hooks/gauge_writer_hook.py, scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py, scripts/mcp_spine_server.py, .mcp.json, examples/**, scripts/install_constellation.py, skills/commander/templates/**
No reaping, expiry, or force-claim of any lease or registry entry
Every ambiguity resolves toward this thing is running (fail-toward-alive)

current_wave.objective: Fix #607 (parent lease heartbeat while blocked) and #525 (namespaced crew scratch directory), owned-files only, no fenced-file edits.
exit_criteria: g1 (#607) implemented, reviewed APPROVE, integrated with a real fresh-process staleness demonstration.
g2 (#525) implemented, reviewed APPROVE, integrated with a real forced-collision demonstration.
Full clean-env cache-cleared suite green at published head.

issues.title: #607 -- parent lease heartbeat while blocked
issues.desired_outcome: A Commander blocked foreground on run_crew.py never reads as engine-lease-stale purely from being blocked.
issues.useful_now: Prevents a force-claim of a spine out from under a running parent -- the exact collision the lease exists to prevent.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: A real checklist_engine.py-backed lease aged past staleness, then a real blocking run_crew.py dispatch, confirmed non-stale afterward in a fresh process.
issues.implementation_latitude: Mechanism chosen: parent-self-heartbeat via checklist_engine.load/heartbeat/save, no self-collision guard, join-before-return ordering.

issues.title: #525 -- namespaced crew scratch directory
issues.desired_outcome: Concurrent crews' evidence/scratch paths no longer collide under generic names; a genuine collision raises rather than silently overwriting.
issues.useful_now: The prior loss was invisible (file exists, parses, describes someone else's gate) -- this makes a collision loud instead.
issues.acceptance_or_falsification_evidence: Two dispatches under distinct tuples get disjoint directories; a forced identical-tuple collision raises CrewLaunchError.
issues.implementation_latitude: Mechanism chosen: scratch_dir() keyed on the full (work_id, gate, role, worktree, attempt) registry tuple, raw-string worktree hash, dispatch-reserves/resume-gets.
hard_constraints_no_gos: run_log_paths itself stays untouched (a related, narrower, pre-existing asymmetry, out of this gate's scope)

wave_forecast.outcome: Follow-up: wire dispatched-crew skills (e.g. skills/reviewer/SKILL.md) to actually write into CREW_SCRATCH_DIR
wave_forecast.why_likely: g2 closes the collision-avoidance half only; the consumption half is a distinct, unowned-files change
entry_conditions: A human/Admiral authorizes the skill-file edit

uncertainty_register.unknown: Whether checklist_engine.save()'s non-atomic write is safe under the new concurrent-writer pattern g1 introduces (parent heartbeat thread + child crew both writing the same shared spine file)
uncertainty_register.affects: Long-term robustness of the #607 fix at scale, not its correctness as measured this run
uncertainty_register.settle_by: A follow-up triage issue against checklist_engine.py (fenced, out of this run's latitude to fix)
uncertainty_register.current_evidence: Reviewer's mutation testing found no observed corruption at the 300s production interval; the risk is structural, not reproduced
uncertainty_register.next_probe: Stress test checklist_engine.save() under concurrent writers, or add atomic-rename write semantics

parked_possibilities: A lease reaper (#552) -- explicitly out of this run's latitude
An explicit blocked-on-child lease state, instead of a heartbeat -- one of #607's three named fix directions, not chosen

completed_outcomes.outcome: Implemented, reviewed (APPROVE), integrated. 7 new tests (ParentLeaseHeartbeatTests). Real fresh-process integration check: an artificially-aged lease read as genuinely stale before the fix (reclaimed stale lease, exit 0) and non-stale after a real blocking dispatch ran with the heartbeat active (REFUSED: checklist already owned by active session, exit 1).
completed_outcomes.evidence: tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k ParentLeaseHeartbeat: 7 passed. Full tests/test_crew_launcher.py: 188 passed. Reviewer's independent mutation test: removed the wraps, confirmed the shared-spine tests fail, restored, confirmed byte-identical diff.

completed_outcomes.outcome: Implemented, reviewed (APPROVE), integrated. 18 new tests. scratch_dir() keys on the full 5-field tuple (work_id, gate, role, worktree, attempt); dispatch reserves via mkdir(exist_ok=False) before any registry write; resume gets without re-reserving. Forced collision raises the exact message naming the path and tuple.
completed_outcomes.evidence: tests/test_crew_launcher.py -k ScratchDir and related: 18 new, 206 total passed. Reviewer's independent mutation test: stripped worktree from the key, confirmed 4 tests fail including the named regression test, restored, confirmed byte-identical diff.

discrepancies.signal: map/INDEX.md went stale mid-run after this run's own new entities (scratch_dir, _parent_lease_heartbeat, and their tests) were added -- MapTreeFreshnessTests failed on the first full-suite run at g2-integrate.
discrepancies.evidence: First full-suite run: 1 failed (test_map_tree_freshness_root_index_matches_a_fresh_build), 3128 passed. Fixed by running `py -m scripts.code_map build --root .` and re-measuring: 3129 passed, 0 failed.
discrepancies.reason: This is expected, mechanical maintenance the launch order's own Inherited Context anticipated ("map/INDEX.md is generated and freshness-tested -- rebuild and commit if entities change") -- repaired in place, not a real defect.

discrepancies.signal: map_orient.py's anchor contract (struct:/capability:/decision: id syntax expecting docs/architecture packets) structurally never matches this repo's own generated map/ (code_map module+entity-count index, no anchor ids), so every commander run against this repo reads DEGRADED-UNPARSEABLE regardless of real staleness.
discrepancies.affects: Every future commander run's context/plan gates in this repo, not this run's own correctness (discharged via the documented substitute path)
discrepancies.reason: A tooling gap worth a dedicated issue, not something this run's latitude covers fixing (map_orient.py is not in File Ownership).

discrepancies.signal: checklist_engine.save() appears to be a non-atomic read-modify-write with no file locking; g1's parent-lease-heartbeat fix introduces a new concurrent writer onto a spine file the dispatched child crew may also write to in the shared-spine case.
discrepancies.affects: Long-term robustness of #607's fix under heavy concurrent write load; no observed corruption this run
discrepancies.evidence: Flagged as tc4 via flag-candidate at g1-review; recorded in this packet's uncertainty_register.
discrepancies.reason: checklist_engine.py is fenced -- out of this run's latitude to fix; a follow-up issue is the correct route.

discrepancies.signal: run_log_paths (scripts/run_crew.py:230-234) omits worktree from its stdout/stderr file naming even though next_attempt/active_duplicate key duplicate-detection on the full (work_id, gate, role, worktree) tuple -- a narrower, pre-existing instance of the same collision shape #525 fixes for scratch dirs.
discrepancies.affects: A latent, narrower collision surface distinct from this run's two named defects
discrepancies.evidence: Found while scoping g2's scratch_dir key tuple against next_attempt's real scoping.
discrepancies.reason: Out of this run's bounded scope (owned files, but a different function than either #607 or #525 named) -- recommend a dedicated follow-up issue rather than a drive-by fix.

discrepancies.signal: #525's CREW_SCRATCH_DIR env var closes the collision-avoidance half only -- run_crew.py cannot make a dispatched reviewer/implementer's own skill actually write into it instead of a shared default.
discrepancies.affects: The real-world completeness of #525's fix outside this run's owned files
discrepancies.evidence: Explicitly named as an honest gap in both the plan gate's mission frame and g2's implementer/reviewer results.
discrepancies.reason: Wiring consuming skills (e.g. skills/reviewer/SKILL.md) is a distinct, unowned-files follow-up, not part of this run's File Ownership.
